entries.mechanism: EUROMOD BE_2025 bun_be (PART SIMULATED, shipped off, switched on for this hypothetical) computes the ordinary first-month unemployment benefit as 0.65 times the post-uprating prior monthly wage, capped only by a stylised 3432.38 EUR/month highwage figure. At this prior wage the cap does not bind, so EUROMOD returns 0.65 x 2532.05 = 1645.83 EUR (bun_s stores this divided by twelve; the oracle bridge annualises it back). The source-backed RuleSpec applies the Royal Decree of 25 November 1991 Article 111 limit A1, which caps the prior DAILY wage at 92.3956 EUR/day, then the Article 114 first-period 65 percent rate over 26 compensable days: 92.3956 x 0.65 x 26 = 1561.49 EUR. The rate is identical; only the cap basis (stylised monthly highwage vs statutory daily A1) differs.

Same structural cap-basis difference as case be-unemployment-single-2400 at a higher prior wage. EUROMOD returns 0.65 x 2954.06 = 1920.14 EUR (highwage cap still not binding); the RuleSpec returns the Article 111 A1 daily-cap-bound 92.3956 x 0.65 x 26 = 1561.49 EUR.

Same structural cap-basis difference at a still higher prior wage, just below EUROMOD's highwage cap. EUROMOD returns 0.65 x 3376.07 = 2194.45 EUR; the RuleSpec returns the Article 111 A1 daily-cap-bound 1561.49 EUR.

At this prior wage EUROMOD's stylised highwage cap binds: the post-uprating prior monthly wage 3798.08 EUR exceeds the 3432.38 EUR/month highwage cap, so EUROMOD returns 0.65 x 3432.38 = 2231.05 EUR and stops rising. The RuleSpec remains at the Article 111 A1 daily-cap-bound 92.3956 x 0.65 x 26 = 1561.49 EUR. The two engines cap at different thresholds (EUROMOD 3432.38 EUR/month vs statutory A1 92.3956 EUR/day), which is the maximum residual of the sweep.
